$sources: The fittings every hanging scroll's mount (装裱) shares, whatever its proportions (the proportions are each work's, in its stage's Hang.json): first values from mounting practice as mounters' manuals and museum photographs of Song, Yuan and Ming scrolls show it; none was measured on the museum's works.
The mount's thickness: the silk (or the painting) laid on two or three layers of backing paper, about 0.3 mm (a mounted scroll rolls up tightly, as only a thin, flexible mount does).
The top stick (天杆): a half-round of about 16 mm across under the heaven's top fold, its flat against the mount's back, so the scroll hangs flat.

The roller (地轴): about 24 mm across, the earth wound on it, weighting the scroll so it hangs straight; its knobs (轴头) about 32 mm across, standing about 35 mm past the mount's edges, turned from a hardwood.
The cord (绦): a silk cord about 3 mm across, tied at two eyes on the stick about a quarter of its length in from each end, and hung over the case's rail or a hook.
